items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-01
items.q: you remember Greenwood and I, uh, got quantities of that wallpaper too.

ctx.x: Well, he talked specifically to us at length about that in the record shop, I think. And Greenwood and I were laughing, you know, and I, I don't remember what it said in the interview now. I've got the, you know, the typescript of the interview even, yeah. Well, he got the book almost at hand. But I don't remember that he got that specific, but he...

He got pretty specific. Well, he didn't think it was too clean, anyhow. Yeah, you know, and this was, this was wallpaper that had been on the wall of a building that had been unoccupied for at least 20 or 30 years. Yeah. And, incidentally, well, you, you remember Greenwood and I, uh, got quantities of that wallpaper too. And I think, I don't know, Johnny, I don't know if Johnny heard about it from us or, or from whom.
I think he went with us one day.

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-07-31
items.q: sometimes Bob Greenwood, sometimes, I think I went to several places with Joan Whitehead

ctx.x: Yeah. In any case, bands then were very willing to audition and to try out. And there was a certain amount of work with private parties going on through people like Myra Menville and Dr. Edmond Suchant. Yeah. And that may have, they may have invited you out there. It would just be the only way I could think of.

I don't, no, I don't think it was one of them. I expect it might come to me, but I don't remember. I know what would happen, you know, would be somebody would, sometimes you, sometimes Bob Greenwood, sometimes, I think I went to several places with Joan Whitehead when she was in New Orleans. Various people would get in touch and say, you know, what's his name is playing out at such and such a place, let's go. And sometimes I'd say, we'll be able to get in, and they'd say, oh sure, the musicians will say it's…

Well, yeah. And, well, and the thing is, the fact is, almost nobody knew about what was going on. As I was saying, much of it was private parties. And things, and Celestan even had a number two band, you mentioned. Yeah. And that was really for playing jobs away from Bourbon Street. He somehow managed to get off. And I would run into them coming out of, say, the St. Charles Hotel. I can remember that one day. And talking to them.

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-02
items.q: Stored all kind of things with me, I don't remember what.

ctx.x: And I think that was probably after Bob had gotten his masters and had been away for a year.
Mm-hmm. Stored all kind of things with me, I don't remember what.
But I think mainly books, not his tapes, but his tape machine. He took them with, uh, yeah, I'm sure he did take that.
